name: The Moss-twined Heart
summary: Near Lake Al'Ameth, Denalan studies a strange heart taken from Blackmoss the Fetid. Dark, oily moss covers the core, yet it keeps beating after being cut from the timberling.

sections.title: A Beating Core
sections.body: Blackmoss the Fetid's heart still pulses after being cut from the timberling. Dark, oily moss hides nearly all of the timberling's core, but a slow rhythm continues within it. That pulse points to a corruption reaching beyond ordinary rot in Teldrassil's wild plants.

sections.title: Denalan's Examination
sections.body: Denalan, a researcher of local flora near Lake Al'Ameth, takes a keen interest in the heart and recognizes its troubling corruption. Timberlings should be gentle beings tied to the boughs of the World Tree, yet this core bears a virulent blight. Troubled by what he sees and eager to understand it, Denalan plans to plant and study the organ, hoping to learn how foul moss takes root in the island's soil.

faq.q: Where does the Moss-twined Heart come from?
aliases: where do i get the heart
faq.answer: The heart comes from Blackmoss the Fetid, a large, heavily corrupted timberling that wanders Teldrassil's wilderness.

faq.q: Why is the heart still beating?
faq.answer: Dark, oily moss appears to keep the heart alive with unnatural vitality. Though cut from the timberling, it continues a slow, steady beat.

Denalan is a night elf naturalist who tends a nursery near Lake Al'Ameth. He devotes himself to studying Teldrassil's flora, its sproutings, and the creeping corruption affecting the island's timberlings.

faq.q: What will Denalan do with the heart?
faq.answer: Denalan plans to plant the heart in an enchanted planter so it can sprout, isolating the foul moss and helping him uncover the cause of the blighted growth.

faq.q: What are timberlings supposed to be?
faq.answer: Timberlings are naturally peaceful plant elementals born of the forest. Dark forces and unnatural taint have driven many of them mad and aggressive across Teldrassil.

faq.q: Is the corruption on the heart magical or natural?
faq.answer: The oily, foul moss suggests an unnatural blight in Teldrassil's native plants, rather than ordinary decay in the wild.

angles.text: As a kaldorei, you see the young World Tree Teldrassil fostering tainted, aggressive timberlings like Blackmoss. Their blight is a sobering sign that your new home is troubled by a creeping sickness.
As a druid, you take keen interest in a beating, blighted heart like this. You seek to learn whether its corruption can be purged or signals deeper rot.
As a student of plants, you can see the oily growth on this core is unnatural. It defies ordinary botanical traits by keeping a severed heart alive.
